# 08. Conversion Rate Optimisation

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Improve business outcomes ethically by reducing friction, increasing trust, and matching calls to action to user intent.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A conversion goal hierarchy covering primary leads, calls, bookings, quote requests, downloads, email signups, local directions, and secondary engagement.
- [ ] A CTA map showing the primary and secondary action for each page type.
- [ ] A trust inventory containing testimonials, certifications, guarantees, process details, pricing signals, policies, portfolio proof, and risk reducers.
- [ ] A form friction standard for field count, required fields, labels, validation, consent, and response expectations.
- [ ] A measurement plan for conversion events using privacy-respecting analytics and consent-aware tracking.
- [ ] A hypothesis backlog for future tests based on observed friction, not random button color changes.
- [ ] A lead quality definition so volume does not become the only optimization target.
- [ ] A post-conversion experience standard for thank-you states, confirmation messages, next steps, and expectation setting.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Conversion paths must be clear without coercive patterns or misleading urgency.
- [ ] Every high-commitment CTA must be supported by enough context and proof to justify the ask.
- [ ] Low-commitment alternatives must exist for users who are interested but not ready to contact.
- [ ] Phone, email, map, and form actions must be accessible and work on mobile.
- [ ] CTA language must describe the outcome, not the interface action alone.
- [ ] Tracking must distinguish meaningful leads from accidental clicks and spam where possible.
- [ ] Static thank-you pages must avoid exposing personal information in URLs.
- [ ] CRO changes must not reduce accessibility, privacy, SEO, or user trust.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check whether users can find pricing, scope, process, timing, service area, and fit criteria before contacting.
- [ ] Check whether proof appears near decision points, not only on a separate testimonials page.
- [ ] Check that forms do not ask for sensitive data unless necessary and legally justified.
- [ ] Check that every CTA has a destination, event name, fallback, and success state.
- [ ] Check that analytics events are named consistently across pages.
- [ ] Check that local business pages support click-to-call, directions, hours, and service area intent.
- [ ] Check that portfolio pages convert by demonstrating capability, not by hiding work behind vague summaries.
- [ ] Check that external booking or form services are free-tier-friendly and have privacy terms reviewed.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid dark patterns, fake scarcity, countdowns without basis, forced opt-ins, and prechecked marketing consent.
- [ ] Avoid placing every CTA at the same visual priority.
- [ ] Avoid optimizing for clicks that create poor-fit leads.
- [ ] Avoid intrusive popups that harm mobile usability or search experience.
- [ ] Avoid hiding contact details behind forms only.
- [ ] Avoid making conversion dependent on third-party scripts that fail silently.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The user should feel informed before being asked to act.
- [ ] Conversion design must increase confidence and reduce risk.
- [ ] The site must support both immediate action and careful evaluation.
- [ ] Every conversion path must be measurable, accessible, privacy-aware, and recoverable.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits to confirm CTA links, form labels, thank-you pages, event attributes, phone links, and privacy references.
- [ ] Use tracking reports to verify that conversion events fire only after consent where required.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Every page has a conversion goal, at least one strong CTA, natural decision-point CTAs, specific labels, primary/secondary hierarchy, footer CTA, final CTA, and easy contact route.
- [ ] CTA strategy includes low-friction and high-intent actions matched to journey stage, hero/header/mobile/final/footer placement, proof-before-ask sequencing, and analytics tracking where used.
- [ ] Contact paths include working form, email, phone, WhatsApp, booking, calendar, map, social message, hero CTA, footer CTA, and no dead-end conversion path.
- [ ] Conversion clarity explains what happens after clicks and submissions, preserves trust near forms, minimizes unnecessary fields, and works on desktop and mobile.
- [ ] Tracking separates CTA clicks from real leads, form starts from submissions, failed submissions from conversions, and payment-link clicks from confirmed purchases.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
